title: Conformational, Aggregation, and Membrane Interaction Dynamics of Keratin-Derived Antimicrobial Peptides from Molecular Dynamics Simulations.
authors: Panagopoulos Papageorgiou, Panagiotis; Karadima, Katerina S; Papageorgiou, Ioanna; Vogiatzis, Georgios G; Mavrantzas, Vlasis G
journal: The journal of physical chemistry. B
one_liner_zh: 该研究通过全原子分子动力学模拟分析角蛋白衍生抗菌肽的构象动态、聚集行为及与膜相互作用，属于蛋白质构象与膜相互作用的计算模拟研究，但对象为抗菌肽而非典型结构预测/设计问题，方法为经典MD模拟。
abstract: Keratin-derived antimicrobial peptides (KAMPs) from human corneal epithelial cells have received considerable attention due to their biocidal activity against both Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria without possessing the conventional characteristics of known antimicrobial peptides (AMPs), such as ordered secondary structure elements and a net positive charge. Here, we perform unbiased, all-atom molecular dynamics (MD) simulations for seven members of the glycine-rich KAMP family and for Pw-Antibac123, which is a distinct keratin-derived peptide obtained through chicken feather hydrolyzates. This study first aims to investigate the structural dynamics of these peptides in dilute and semidilute aqueous solutions. Our results verify the noncanonical structure of KAMPs and validate the molecular model of Pw-Antibac123 that has been proposed in the literature. Increasing the peptide concentration in the aqueous solution leads to self-assembly and peptide aggregation, due to the development of interpeptide hydrogen bonds and the strong effect of electrostatic interactions. The effect of intermolecular amino acid interactions on the secondary structure of KAMPs is also discussed, allowing us to identify strong synergies between specific amino acid pairs, such as serine and glycine, valine and leucine, and arginine and isoleucine. Subsequently, we focus on how KAMP-18C, an 18-residue-long KAMP, interacts with model Gram-positive lipid bilayers. Since spontaneous aggregation is not observed, we construct artificial pores and embed peptides within the membrane to assess the stability of these systems. We discuss how our findings correlate with proposed mechanisms of action for AMPs.
abstract_zh: 来自人角膜上皮细胞的角蛋白衍生抗菌肽（KAMPs）因其对革兰氏阳性菌和革兰氏阴性菌均具有杀菌活性而受到广泛关注，尽管它们不具备已知抗菌肽（AMPs）的常规特征，如有序二级结构元件和净正电荷。在此，我们对甘氨酸丰富的KAMP家族中的七个成员以及Pw-Antibac123（一种通过鸡羽毛水解产物获得的独特角蛋白衍生肽）进行了无偏的全原子分子动力学（MD）模拟。本研究首先旨在探讨这些肽在稀溶液和半稀水溶液中的结构动力学。我们的结果验证了KAMPs的非经典结构，并证实了文献中提出的Pw-Antibac123分子模型。提高水溶液中的肽浓度会导致自组装和肽聚集，这是由于肽间氢键的形成以及静电相互作用的强烈影响。我们还讨论了分子间氨基酸相互作用对KAMPs二级结构的影响，从而识别出特定氨基酸对之间的强协同作用，如丝氨酸和甘氨酸、缬氨酸和亮氨酸、以及精氨酸和异亮氨酸。随后，我们重点研究了KAMP-18C（一种由18个残基组成的KAMP）如何与模型革兰氏阳性脂质双层相互作用。由于未观察到自发聚集，我们构建了人工孔道并将肽嵌入膜内，以评估这些系统的稳定性。我们讨论了我们的发现如何与AMPs的拟议作用机制相关联。
